description: Two-pointer in-place alphanumeric filtering with O(n) time and O(1) space.

transcript.text: Hi! The problem asks to verify if a string is a palindrome considering only alphanumeric characters and ignoring cases. An intuitive way is creating a new cleaned string, but that requires O(n) extra memory. Instead, we can use two pointers: left starting at 0, right at s.length - 1.
How do the two pointers handle non-alphanumeric characters?

While left < right, we skip non-alphanumeric characters by advancing left or decrementing right. When both point to valid characters, we compare them in lower case. If they mismatch, return false. If loop finishes, return true.
Excellent. What is the space complexity?
Space complexity is O(1) auxiliary space because we do not allocate any new strings or arrays, just two integer indices.
